extracted.intended_audience: members of Parliament, parliamentary committees, policymakers, and officials responsible for the governance of British India
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and records statutory powers, committee evidentiary standards, and administrative recommendations for investigating and managing Indian revenues and alleged abuses (includes bill clauses, witness examination rules, and committee management proposals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners' powers and duties (Mr Pitt's Bill, Clause No.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioners, or any two of them, are empowered and required to examine upon oath persons of all descriptions and any other persons they think fit touching the business of each office/department, and the fees, gratuities, perquisites, and emoluments taken therein; and all such persons are required punctually to attend and to observe and execute such orders and directions as the commissioners shall make or give.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes authority to administer oaths; require attendance of any persons 'of all descriptions' and 'all other persons' they judge fit; and to issue orders and directions for the purposes of the act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to investigate corrupt and fraudulent practices and to compel production of records
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioners, or any two of them, are empowered to examine into any corrupt and fraudulent practices or other misconduct committed by persons concerned in the management of the specified offices or departments, and are authorized to send precepts under their hands and seals for any person or persons whatsoever, and for such books, papers, writings, or records as they shall judge necessary for their information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioners may meet with or without adjournment and may require bailiffs, constables, sheriffs, and other His Majesty's officers to obey and execute their orders and precepts; the clause ties investigative authority to compulsory access to documentary evidence and to enforcement through Crown officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative remit: examine fees, gratuities, perquisites, emoluments and related abuses
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory remit explicitly charges the commissioners to inquire into the Fees, Gratuities, Perquisites, Emoluments which are, or have been lately, received in the several public offices mentioned, and to examine into any Abuses which may exist in the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This delineates the subject-matter of inquiry (remuneration and incidental emoluments in public offices) and frames abuses of such emoluments as within the commission's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for assessing the Nabob of Arcot's debts (Appendix No.2 witness examination topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the Nabob's debts should distinguish older debts (pre-1766) from newer debts (post-1766), estimate principal amounts, determine whether debts were actually advanced in money/goods or constituted obligations for services, verify Court of Directors' approval/recognition, and assess punctuality and rate of interest paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific investigative points used in witness examination include: approximate amounts (e.g., twenty‑three/sixty lacs of pagodas), whether interest exceeded the statutory 12% cap (and whether higher rates were customary prior to the Act of Parliament), whether parts of the debt were fictitious obligations for services, and corroboration by settlement persons or documentary evidence; examples include Mr Smith's testimony about discounts offered (24% vs statutory 12%) and the timeliness of interest payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on assignment/mortgage/pledge of native territory to British subjects (India Bill / Mr Fox's Bill, Appendix No.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Native protected princes (e.g., Nabob of Arcot, Rajah of Tanjore) shall not assign, mortgage, or pledge any territory or land or the produce/revenue thereof to any British subject; any such assignment/mortgage/pledge to a British subject is declared null and void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a remedial mechanism: payments or deliveries made under any such void assignment may be recovered back by the native prince from the person receiving them (or their representatives). This is an explicit legal prohibition and recovery right intended to prevent transfer of native territorial revenue to British private interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee recommendations for management of assigned revenue (Committee of Assigned Revenue, 27 May 1782)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations to remedy mismanagement of the Carnatic include: collect and digest transactions for clarity; propose immediate and considerable reductions of expenses; effect a total change of principal aumildars where necessary; farm out rentable districts by public advertisement; advertise for the whole period of the Nabob's assignment; promise full Company protection to encourage bidders; and appoint renters under the Company's sole authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: post‑war devastation and predatory local management left revenues unrecoverable under prior systems. Operational guidance: prefer retrenching too much rather than too little (easier to add later), remove extraordinary charges (sibbendies, sepoys, horsemen) from accounts where Company enlists or discharges these forces, and use public competitive bidding circulated throughout provinces to increase receipts. Also emphasises gathering materials to know the former and present state of the country before larger reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity and perpetual parliamentary responsibility as checks on abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: The report asserts that the 'better part' of the proposed establishment is the publicity of its proceedings and its perpetual responsibility to Parliament; public oversight and parliamentary cognizance are presented as essential checks against tyranny, rapine, and the abuse of delegated power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a governance principle: without public scrutiny and accountability to Parliament, remote delegated authority tends toward corruption and will prevent redress of grievances; hence transparency in proceedings and continual parliamentary responsibility are recommended institutional safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for detecting clandestine and collusive practice: combination and comparison of circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Clandestine and collusive practices can only be traced by combination and comparison of circumstances; rejecting such combination/comparison rejects the primary means of detecting fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames an investigative method: cross‑referencing multiple facts and circumstances and comparing them to detect patterns of collusion or concealment, rather than relying on single isolated facts or confessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary sources and documentary practice relied on by the committee/debate
rubrics_metrics.description: The inquiry and debate rely on printed papers of correspondence, Select Committee reports and appendices, witness examinations, letters, and published consultations and proceedings as the evidentiary foundation for findings and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes and references (Select Committee reports, Madras consultations, letters, printed appendices) are repeatedly cited as the material basis for assertions; the committee both collects primary documentary records and uses public printing to ensure the facts are 'in every hand.'
